sentiment.rationale: The document reports a GAAP loss per share of ($7.02) for Q4 2021, a significant improvement from ($14.65) in Q4 2020, and operating cash flow turned positive at $0.7 billion. However, forward guidance is effectively lowered by a $3.5 billion pre-tax non-cash charge on the 787 program, with management stating that rework will take longer than previously expected, causing further delivery delays. This structural risk (ongoing 787 production and delivery issues) outweighs the positive cash flow inflection, leading to a bearish score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2021 revenue of $14.8 billion, down 3% from $15.3 billion in Q4 2020. Full-year 2021 revenue of $62.3 billion, up 7% from $58.2 billion in 2020.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($7.02) for Q4 2021, compared to ($14.65) in Q4 2020. Core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($7.69) for Q4 2021, compared to ($15.25) in Q4 2020.
summary.guidance: The 737 program is currently producing at 26 per month and progressing towards 31 per month in early 2022. The 787 program is producing at a very low rate until deliveries resume, with an expected gradual return to five per month over time. The company now anticipates 787 abnormal costs will increase to approximately $2 billion, with most being incurred by the end of 2023.
summary.margin: Q4 2021 GAAP operating margin of (28.2)%, compared to (52.6)% in Q4 2020. Core (non-GAAP) operating margin of (30.7)%, compared to (54.7)% in Q4 2020.
key_risks: 787 program recorded a $3.5 billion pre-tax non-cash charge; rework will take longer than previously expected, causing further delivery delays.
Defense, Space & Security operating margin decreased to (4.4)% due to lower volume and a $402 million pre-tax charge on the KC-46A Tanker program.
Global Services operating margin negatively impacted by a $220 million inventory impairment.
Cash and marketable securities decreased to $16.2 billion from $20.0 billion at the beginning of the quarter, primarily driven by debt repayment.
The company continues to face risks related to the COVID-19 pandemic, 737 MAX regulatory approvals, and overall health of the aircraft production system.
key_opportunities: Continued global return to service of 737 MAX, including progress in China with the Civil Aviation Administration of China issuing an airworthiness directive in December.
Over 300,000 revenue flights completed on 737 MAX since FAA approval, with fleet reliability above 99%.
Robust commercial orders, including 164 737 MAX and 24 freighter aircraft in Q4.
Total backlog of $377 billion, including $297 billion for Commercial Airplanes.
Global Services revenue increased 15% and operating margin increased to 9.3% driven by higher commercial volume.
